svg.title: First ionisation energies
svg.desc: A graph of first ionisation energy against atomic number for hydrogen to calcium, showing peaks at the noble gases, drops at the alkali metals, and dips at boron, aluminium, oxygen and sulfur, with explanations.
svg.text: First ionisation energies, H to Ca

g.data-info: The energy needed to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Generally increases: nuclear charge increases while the electrons are added to the same shell, so they are held more tightly.
From a noble gas to the next alkali metal (He → Li, Ne → Na, Ar → K): the electron is in a new shell, further from the nucleus and more shielded.
The electron removed is in a p sub-level, slightly higher in energy (and more shielded) than the s electrons before it.
The electron removed is paired in a p orbital; repulsion between the paired electrons makes it easier to remove.
